kernel.governing_law: The speaker commands a terrain of surplus and scarcity simultaneously — everything acquired cheaply, intoxicants everywhere, velocity outrunning sense — asserting mastery through excess that is indistinguishable from waste.
kernel.mutated_relation: The cost of each abundance made primary: what was spent, lost, or forfeited so that the surplus could appear at all — the debt-face of every free thing.

independent.recovered_law: In Text A, items are acquired freely or cheaply and consumed/enjoyed in abundance (things flow toward the subject at no cost). In Text B, every acquisition incurs debt, cost, or bodily sacrifice (things flow toward the subject only through obligation and loss).
independent.law_match_note: Both describe the same structural change: free/costless abundance is rewritten so that every surplus now carries an explicit cost, debt, or sacrifice as its precondition.
independent.terminal_note: The final lines sustain the debt/cost inversion ('pre-spent,' 'broker off a tab'), never reverting to Text A's free-abundance framing.
